messages:
emma_support: customer reports invoice ~3x higher than their local SDK estimator. they sent a simple chat payload and says sdk shows ~120 tokens but invoice charges ~380. attaching minimal repro.
liam_backend: can you paste their exact request body? maybe system messages or tool outputs are being injected server-side.
emma_support: here — they used our JS SDK with function calling enabled, minimal messages:
```json
{
  "model": "open-llama-2-13b",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this doc: ..."}
  ],
  "functions": [{"name":"search_docs", "parameters":{}}],
  "stream": false
}
```
emma_support: they said they disabled function calls on client but server policy enables a sidecar tool. billing spike coincides with sidecar activity.
liam_backend: if sidecar injects tool call metadata (prefill/tool-run context) that can add tokens. also server may attach a short hidden prompt preface with routing info. will check logs for that request id. @metering-bot any flags?
metering-bot: detected 2026-11-08T12:13:20Z spike for customer acct: +260 tokens per chat on average for calls tagged "sidecar-prefill". audit-id: mtr-17688-01
kevin_engineer: possible sources: 1) server-side system prompts 2) tool outputs (kv metadata) appended to assistant stream 3) function call signatures included in the request body that get tokenized for billing. did they call functions?

sophia_billing: invoice shows those conversations billed under "api:chat.complete" with extra 250 tokens each. ledger samples attached. customers insist they didn't receive that content in UI.
emma_support: customer says UI shows only the assistant summary and nothing else; they recorded the websocket traffic from SDK and claim nothing extra arrived.
liam_backend: common pattern: we count tokens on the server after we expand tool outputs or add internal preface, but streaming client may stop before those tokens are emitted to the user (stream cutoff). if the runtime executed a tool and then trimmed the final assistant content for UI, the billing still counts the generated tool/assistant tokens.

kevin_engineer: quick repro suggestion for support to run server-side trace: set env REDWOOD_TRACE=1 then replay the exact request id. log will show prefill and tool payloads. also grep for "_runtime_prefill" and "_kv_meta" markers.
emma_support: forwarded steps to customer. they repro'd once with trace enabled and attached trace id trace-17688-cust. results below.
--- trace excerpt ---
PREFILL (server): "[route=us-west|tier=free|sid=acct-123] system: internal-routing v=1"
ASSISTANT: generated summary tokens=115
TOOL_CALL: search_docs -> returned 3 hits (kv-metadata size=210 tokens)
ASSISTANT (post-tool): appended 145 tokens for step-by-step extraction
--- end excerpt ---

emma_support: that pretty much explains the delta: sdk estimate only counted the visible assistant chunk (115) while invoice counts everything generated including tool returns and server prefill (~115+210+145=470). customer sentiment: upset because they didn't expect hidden tool return tokens to be billed.
sophia_billing: policy: we bill for anything generated by the model, even tool outputs and server prefaces. but we should improve transparency. propose adding a per-call breakdown in the console: prefill, tool-output, assistant-visible.
liam_backend: short-term: we can surface a header in the response like x-redwood-metering-breakdown: prefill=25;tools=210;visible=115 so SDKs can surface it. long-term: audit SDK estimator to optionally include server-prefill and tool-output heuristics.
kevin_engineer: also note function-calling can produce JSON schemas that increase client-side tokenizer counts if included — double-check we aren't echoing function signatures back into prompt during debug.
emma_support: customer accepted explanation but asked for two actions: 1) refund for past 24 hours spike 2) flag behavior in docs and expose breakdown header. can billing do one-off credit?
sophia_billing: will authorize a partial credit for the 24h spike while docs/update is implemented. filing a follow-up to product: PROD-6243 to add breakdown header and console UI.
liam_backend: I'll add a lightweight middleware to emit x-redwood-metering-breakdown for the next deploy. tagging @kevin_engineer to review.
kevin_engineer: ack, I'll draft PR with opt-in flag and tests for token accounting.
emma_support: thanks team :pray:, closing customer loop now and cc-ing them on PROD-6243 and refund timeline.
